editorial.headline: Wholesale Vegetable Trading: Open Nationally, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Wholesale vegetable trading is open nationally at every business scale, but PMA registration in Bali is blocked under the province’s permanent moratorium.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this wholesale vegetable-trading activity in Bali today. That is the practical conclusion of Bali’s province-wide, permanent moratorium for PMA registrations in activities assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk. The national position is more open: the activity is open to foreign investment, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%.

The activity itself is straightforward and specific: wholesale trade in vegetables, including spinach, water spinach and cabbage. It concerns the commercial distribution of those goods at wholesale level—the point at which vegetable supply moves through trade rather than being described as retailing, cultivation or processing. The classification is therefore anchored in the trade of vegetables as products, with those named examples giving the scope its practical shape.

The record permits registration at Micro, Small, Medium and Large scales. That breadth matters nationally because it makes the activity available across the full stated range of business sizes, rather than reserving it for one class of enterprise. For PMA, the national setting is equally direct: it is marked open and carries a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling under the cited presidential regulations. National openness, however, is not the same as a Bali registration route.

In Bali, the activity is blocked for PMA because its OSS risk assessment at the Large scale is Low or Medium-Low across every scope. Bali’s moratorium, effective from 13 May 2026, blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA on an island-wide and permanent basis. The result is an unusually clear divide: nationally, foreign ownership may reach the stated ceiling; in Bali, PMA registration for this activity is unavailable under the current moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not create a Bali registration route where the province’s permanent PMA moratorium applies.
